study type: Randomized controlled trial (human infants), Experimental mouse model study
exposure: Colonization with transitional stool from vaginally seeded infants vs. control (placebo) seeded infants (germ-free mice)
cohort: Germ-free mice were colonized with transitional stool from human infants who received vaginal seeding or control (placebo) seeding in a double-blind randomized trial.
finding: Male mice colonized with stool from vaginally seeded infants showed a reduction in intraabdominal adipose tissue (IAAT) volume compared to control mice, suggesting that early changes in the gut microbiome and metabolome caused by vaginal seeding positively impact metabolic health.
mod_finding: Vaginal seeding in C-section infants led to gut microbiome and metabolome changes that, when transplanted to mice, decreased intraabdominal adiposity, suggesting a positive impact on metabolic health related to mimicking vaginal birth.
